source.display_title:
05/03/2026 - Omar Maldy & Farooq Bey - Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
 — Follow Up

call.sequence_note: Explicitly a second conversation. The rep opens with 'obviously you and I, spoke yesterday. Just kind of picking up from where we left off' and later apologises for repeating a question — 'Sorry, sorry, sorry, I forgot I did. I've taken 10 other calls today' — to which the prospect replies 'So you asked that yesterday.' The prior call, presumably dated 05/02/2026, is not in this batch, so any Baseline or discovery run there is unobserved.

prospect.name: Omar Maldonado
prospect.location: United States, Central time zone (city never stated)
prospect.occupation: Not explicitly stated. Works with young people and has coworkers — 'I'd be able to get stronger and gain strength for my coworkers and for the youth that I work with' — in a workplace that serves him breakfast and lunch five days a week. Gardens and keeps a dog.
prospect.training_background: Never established. The rep did not ask what he currently does, what he has tried, or whether he trains at all. The only training-adjacent statement is his own assessment that '30 minutes, three to four times a week, like that's easy, like, are you kidding me?'

signals: PROPOSED LABEL: the_deliberator. High stated internal readiness with no physical or medical driver at all, blocked by two things the existing avatars do not describe — a genuine liquidity ceiling and a decision style that requires reviewing written options off-call. He is not recovering from anything and not optimising anything; the purchase is framed almost entirely as a test of his own follow-through.
Explicitly names the problem as character rather than body: 'being used to failing... I don't continue to try when it gets hard', 'I'm comfortable with average'
Faith-framed motivation throughout: 'Most important in my life now is my relationship with my higher power, my relationship with God', 'I know that I'm called for a higher purpose'
Not the_rebuilder: there is no lost former self, no illness, no injury and no prior peak being chased — the direction is toward a person he says he has not yet been
Not skeptical_bargain_hunter: he anchors to cheap alternatives late and reactively (Primal University, YouTube) rather than arriving with one that worked
Decision style is the defining trait and he states it plainly: 'if I lay all my options out, and think through each option clearly, not on a call, not on video, that, to me, seems more like who I am'

goals.text: Become disciplined — wake earlier, do the morning things that make him comfortable in himself from the start of the day
Close the gap between knowing and doing — 'it's not just about hearing, it's about doing'
Get stronger so he can use his body for others — for his coworkers and the youth he works with
Be able to garden and take his dog on more walks
Repair the areas his pattern has damaged — friendships, relationships, family, work, and above all his relationship with God
Higher vitality and better health generally, carried over from the first call
Know exactly what to eat each day rather than being handed macro ranges — 'just tell me what I'm going to do, I'll do it'

pains.text: Quits when things get hard and has done so his whole life — 'I don't continue to try. If it's too hard, I just get used to it'
Adaptability turned against him — 'I'm very flexible, and I say that that is one of my strengths. Unfortunately, it becomes a downfall when I'm able to get used to things that shouldn't be'
Comfortable with average and aware of it — 'I don't have to, so not striving for it to be a need... because I'm comfortable with average'
Says it has cost him friendships, relationships, closeness with family, and literal jobs
Spiritual cost he ranks above all the others — 'Knowing to do something and choosing to not do it' has damaged his relationship with God
Eats whatever is put in front of him — breakfast and lunch are provided at work five days a week and 'it's healthier, but it's not optimal for what I want for my body'
Has the knowledge and does not act on it — 'I have the knowledge of what I'm supposed to eat. Unfortunately, I eat whatever is there for me'
Financially constrained — $500 to $700 a month is his stated capacity and paying a three-month tier up front would, by his own account, impact him
Distrusts his own follow-through, which is why he scored the offer 8 rather than 10 — 'Because I know people, and I know myself'

objections.raw_quote: Yes, I'm ready. And I also know my finances aren't ready.
objections.rep_response: Asked permission, then ran the financial-picture questions — cash on hand, monthly capacity, credit score — and returned with financed monthly figures

objections.raw_quote: Price is a little high than what I would want, especially for a month trial. Because that's kind of, when you said the month trial, I was like, alright, I can give it a month trial. But even that is a little steep.
objections.rep_response: Countered with a seriousness frame — 'What are you going to be more serious about? Something that's 50 bucks or something that's actually showing a serious commitment from yourself?'

objections.raw_quote: Six is about my cap of what I'm willing to pay, yeah.
objections.rep_response: Offered $650/mo, was told 'that would be stretching what I'm willing to pay, but $650 is doable', and answered 'Well, I don't want you to be comfortable'

objections.raw_quote: So that's 60 people that have Trevor's number and are reaching out to him at any point in the day. That's a lot of people... Is Trevor able to, has he taken too much on, or is that the type of person he is?
objections.rep_response: Explained that touchpoints are high in months two and three and taper by months four to six, and that the model is designed to make clients independent

objections.raw_quote: For right now, I'm not willing to commit to anything specifically. Um, I would want to look at some, some options and, and see what I can do.
objections.rep_response: Probed the reason, offered a $100 token deposit, was refused, then challenged the stated reason directly

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, I'm not gonna make any decisions today. Um, this is something that I kind of want to think about.
objections.rep_response: Asked 'want me to be honest with you or nice?' and told him 'You and I both know that's some BS, brother', then ran an extended challenge sequence on comfort and capability

objections.raw_quote: I'm not the type of person to put stuff on credit card. That's just not who I am as a, as a person.
objections.rep_response: Later walked him step by step into Klarna, a buy-now-pay-later credit facility, which the prospect identified himself: 'this is basically a credit card, dude. APR 13.99, that's wild.'

offer.payment_plan_terms: Structured live and repeatedly re-cut. In-house / Paver options quoted: 12-month tier at $975/mo over 12 months (total $11,700 against a $9,000 sticker); 6-month tier at either 6 x $1,200 (total $7,200) or 12 x $650 (total $7,800) against a $6,000 sticker; 3-month tier at 3 x $1,533 (total $4,600), 6 x $800 (total $4,800) or 12 x $433 (total $5,200) against a $4,000 sticker. Klarna was then offered as an alternative at 13.99% APR over three to 24 months. A $100 token deposit was also proposed to hold the deal pending a further call. Nothing was accepted.

evidence: No payment, no agreement and no deposit. The $100 token deposit was explicitly declined: 'what I'm going to do is I'm going to take some time and think about this, without putting in a hundred dollar deposit'
Final position stated plainly: 'I'm currently not able to or capable of doing any of the options until I review them'
A further sales call was booked for 3 p.m. Central the following Sunday, plus a midweek WhatsApp check-in — 'I've sent you an invite for 3 p.m.'
Intent is genuine and repeatedly stated: 'I want it, and, not but, I want to make sure that I'm making the right choice'

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: the last substantive exchange has the prospect conceding under pressure rather than agreeing — 'If I feel this much of push, then yeah, clearly, I'm not capable' — which makes the booked follow-up less solid than the calendar invite suggests

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: the rep himself offered the disqualifying path, 'if you don't have the capability, Omar, generally, dude, I will tell you, don't do this, save up, come in for Primal University', which the prospect thanked him for twice
outcome.next_step: Rep to check in midweek on WhatsApp and reconvene Sunday at 3 p.m. Central; prospect to review the Paver and Klarna links and decide between the one, three, six and twelve month options

notable.note: The longest and most difficult call in the batch, and the one with the most for a principal to look at. Discovery and the consequence frame were genuinely excellent — the route A / route B question and the want-versus-need sequence are the best-run phases in this folder. Everything after price collapsed. The rep laid out four tiers and then three financing schedules across two lenders, creating the exact analysis paralysis the prospect then cited as his reason for not deciding, and told him so as feedback: 'because so many options were laid out, now I have to kind of go through each option'. Financed totals run $600 to $2,700 above sticker and were described as 'a little bit of interest'. The prospect stated twice that he does not use credit cards on principle and was then walked click by click into a 13.99% APR Klarna facility. After a clear decline the rep told him his stated reason was 'BS', invented a $100 deposit with no benefit to the buyer, and pressed for a further twenty minutes until the prospect said 'If I feel this much of push, then yeah, clearly, I'm not capable.' To the rep's credit, he did also offer the honest disqualification — save up and take Primal University instead. Roughly twenty minutes of the call are missing from the recording.

quality.notes: Severe. Whole passages invert, including the closing sequence where the rep's lines — 'first and foremost, I'm a coach... I do a bit of life coaching on the side', 'As a coach, I don't want you to be comfortable', 'I've been on this earth for 39 years', and 'if you don't have the capability, Omar, generally, dude, I will tell you, don't do this' — are all attributed to Omar.Maldonado. Roles were resolved from content; the 39-year age statement belongs to the rep, not the prospect, who is 36. A block of roughly ninety seconds at 01:38:47 to 01:39:38 is then repeated verbatim at 01:40:02 to 01:41:00 with the labels shifted. There is also a recording gap of about twenty minutes between 00:41:26 and 01:01:31, acknowledged on the tape as 'before it got cut off'. One garbled line at 00:08:31, 'I think partially my wife', is most likely 'part of my psyche' and was NOT treated as evidence of a spouse. Duration is wall-clock and includes the gap.
